prompt:

Given the following forecast for SBIN (base year 2021):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2021,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2022,
      "revenue_cr": 332000,
      "net_income_cr": 24500,
      "eps": 27.45
    },
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 362000,
      "net_income_cr": 29000,
      "eps": 32.5
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 394000,
      "net_income_cr": 34000,
      "eps": 38.1
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Credit growth recovers to 10-12% YoY post-pandemic as economic activity normalises, driving interest income higher, while investment income normalises from elevated FY2021 levels, yielding blended Total Income CAGR of ~9% over FY2022-24.",
    "Net Profit margin expansion continues as NPA provisioning requirements decline sharply from the elevated FY2020-21 cycle (Gross NPA fell from ~\u20b91,49,092 cr to ~\u20b91,26,389 cr), with credit costs normalising and deferred tax credit tailwinds partially reversing, supporting PAT CAGR of ~19% over FY2022-24."
  ],
  "reasoning": "For SBI (a bank/NBFC), Total Income = Interest Earned + Other Income is used as the Revenue line. FY2021 consolidated Total Income = \u20b9278,115 cr (Interest Earned) + \u20b9107,222 cr (Other Income) = \u20b9385,337 cr; FY2020 = \u20b9269,852 cr + \u20b998,159 cr = \u20b9368,011 cr, implying ~4.7% YoY growth \u2014 however the standalone segment data shows Total Income of ~\u20b9308,647 cr (FY21) vs \u20b9302,545 cr (FY20), roughly 2% growth per the Directors' Report. Using the consolidated figures from schedules 13 and 14, FY2021 Total Income is ~\u20b9385,337 cr vs FY2020 ~\u20b9368,011 cr (~4.7% YoY). FY2021 is anomalous: interest income on advances fell (loan growth was muted in COVID year, rate cuts compressed yields), while investment income surged on bond gains; NPA provisioning remained very high (~\u20b929,759 cr standalone). The anomaly flag is set because the revenue growth was suppressed and profit growth was distorted by one-off deferred tax credits (~\u20b93,749 cr) and lower-than-normal credit costs versus FY2020. Using a 3-year CAGR basis is not fully possible from the text (only two years of P&L data provided), so I use the ~4-5% revenue CAGR implied and adjust upward to ~9% for FY2022 onward as credit demand recovers post-pandemic, interest rates normalise/rise (RBI tightening cycle expected), and SBI's large deposit franchise re-prices. Net profit trajectory is anchored by declining provisioning drag and improving RoA (0.48% in FY2021, trending toward 0.6-0.65%), driving PAT from \u20b920,410 cr to ~\u20b934,000 cr by FY2024. EPS is computed on the stable share count of 892.46 crore shares."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:

  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}

}
